name: Panzaleo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Montaluisa Chasiquiza, Luis. 2019. La estandarizacion ortografica del quichua ecuatoriano. Consideraciones historicas, dialectologicas y sociolinguisticas. Quito: Abya-Yala (CC BY-NC-SA). Section 'Lengua panzaleo', pp. 63-70ff.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Surveys the history of the Panzaleo question (Jijon y Caamano's 3,398 names; Paz y Mino's 562 names in 82 groups by ending; Reino 1988; Costales 2002 denial) and lists toponym endings -alo/-halo, -asi, -coa, -chi, -gua, -lagua, -leo, -luisa, -li, -mala, -mbo, -pi, -po, -to, -toa, -tug, -yambo with examples.

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F. H. 2012. Languages of the Middle Andes in areal-typological perspective: Emphasis on Quechuan and Aymaran. In L. Campbell & V. Grondona (eds.), The Indigenous Languages of South America: A Comprehensive Guide, 575-624. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton (OAPEN open access).
sources.note: Nothing. Panzaleo named only as one of the extinct intra-Andean Ecuadorian languages attested through 'voluminous toponym data' (Jijon y Caamano 1940-1945; Paz y Mino 1940-1942, 1961); 'for Panzaleo, Puruha and Canar no connection with any surviving language could be established'.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Cestmir. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. pp. 245-246 (Panzaleo entry and Andaqui/Paez/Panzaleo comparative wordlist).
sources.note: Nothing. Entry reads: 'Panzaleo or Latacunga or Quito - extinct language once spoken in the provinces of Pichincha, Cotopaxi and Tunguragua, Ecuador. [Jijon y Caamano 1919, pp. 370-372, 1927, pp. 193-197, 1941-1947, vol. 1, pp. 286-396; Paz y Mino 1941b.]' plus a 12-item unglossed comparative list.

sources.citation: Coba Robalino, Jose Maria. 1929. Monografia general del canton Pillaro. Quito: Prensa Catolica.
sources.note: Nothing. Amateur Paez/Panzaleo etymologising of local names; no phonological remarks.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 panz1235 (https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/panz1235); Wikipedia 'Panzaleo language' (en) and 'Idioma panzaleo' (es); Wikidata Q3123275.
sources.note: Glottolog lists zero references. Both Wikipedia articles give only the toponymic endings (-(h)alo, -leo, -lagua/-ragua) and the Loukotka/Jijon Paez hypothesis; no phonology.

sources.citation: Urban, Matthias. 2023. Linguistic Stratigraphy: Recovering Traces of Lost Languages in the Central Andes. Cham: Springer.
